chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both,

that he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, was asked about in what salvation lies tomorrow, and he said: Salvation is only in that you do not attempt to deceive Allah, by which He makes him in deception, for indeed, the one who attempts to deceive Allah, He will make him in deception and strip him of faith, and he would be deceiving himself, if he sensed it. It was then said to him: And how does one attempt to deceive Allah? He said: That one does what Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has ordered, and then intends with it other than Him. Hence, beware from ostentation, for indeed, it is to assign partners to Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. Indeed, an ostentator will be called on the Day of Resurrection by four names: «O disbeliever, O dissolute, O treacherous, O looser! Your deed are wasted and your reward is invalidated, and you will have no good quality today. Hence, seek your reward from the one you acted for.»

key_terms.الرِّيَاءُ: Ostentation or showing off in worship

ai.seo_question: How does riya' (ostentation) lead to deception of Allah and loss of faith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'deceiving Allah' refers to *riya'* (ostentation), where one performs obligatory acts with the intent of gaining human praise rather than divine pleasure. This subtle form of *shirk* invalidates the reward, as the Mura'i (one who shows off) is called forth on Judgment Day with four titles: *Kafir, Fajir, Ghadir,* and *Khasir*, having lost their true Creator's favor. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the purity of intention (*ikhlas*) as the cornerstone of accepted worship.
